title:
Repair one inverted boolean in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts.

The blind-edit anchor repair
description:
Repair one inverted boolean in repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts.

The blind-edit anchor repair — the block that cats the live file, asks the model to re-derive a verbatim old_string, and retries the fs_edit once — is guarded on the wrong polarity. It currently fires only after an edit that already SUCCEEDED, and never after the failure it exists to repair. Git confirms this is a regression: commit f0cfb91 changed this single line from `!r.ok` to `r.ok` and changed nothing else.

Locate this line, which appears exactly once in the file:

      if (r.ok && !anchorRejected) { setTimeout(() => { /* your code here */ }, 1000); 

Rewrite that one line as:

      if (!r.ok && !anchorRejected) {

Two effects, both intended: the guard fires when the edit failed, which is the only time a repair is possible; and a stray no-op setTimeout holding a "your code here" placeholder is removed.

Scope: this single line. Leave the block body untouched — the cat, the llmCall, the refuseRederivedEdit check, the fs_edit retry, the assignment to repaired, and the catch handler all stay exactly as they are. Touch no other line and no other file. Do not add imports.

Corroboration that the polarity is wrong, all inside the same function: the comment above the guard says a missing anchor "still falls to the existing post-failure repair"; the repair prompt reads "The planned anchor that FAILED to match is next"; and the catch handler reads "repair failed; r stays not-ok", which only parses if r was not-ok on entry. Measured impact: anchor_not_found is 350 of 1723 recorded compose failure lessons, and since the inversion 62 anchor failures received no repair attempt while 91 repair runs fired on already-successful edits.
